pull.title: KAFKA-21380: Move limit-reached records to ARCHIVING on failed transition rollback
pull.body:
### JIRA
https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/KAFKA-21380

### Problem

When the DLQ flow is enabled for a share group (KIP-1191), records whose delivery count reaches the limit are moved to `ARCHIVING` on the normal release path so they are written to the DLQ topic (`InFlightState.tryUpdateState` with `dlqSupportEnabled=true`).

However, the rollback path in `InFlightState.completeStateTransition(false)` - taken when a two-phase state transition fails (e.g. the persister write fails) and the acquisition lock has expired - archives the records directly:

```java
state = previousState.deliveryCount() >= rollbackState.maxDeliveryCount ?
    RecordState.ARCHIVED : RecordState.AVAILABLE;
```

This bypasses the DLQ flow entirely: records that should have been dead-lettered are silently archived and never appear in the DLQ topic. Note that `completeStateTransition(boolean)` has no access to the `dlqSupportEnabled` flag, so the rollback path cannot currently reach `ARCHIVING`.

Two related inconsistencies:

1. `ARCHIVING` (normal path) vs `ARCHIVED` (rollback path) for the same limit-reached condition.
2. The normal path evaluates the limit with the delivery count including the current delivery (`deliveryCount` incremented before the check), while the rollback path uses `previousState.deliveryCount()` - the counts differ by one.

### Fix

- Thread the DLQ-support flag through `completeStateTransition`; on rollback with an expired lock and the delivery count at the limit, records move to `ARCHIVING` when DLQ is enabled (mirroring `tryUpdateState`), otherwise to `ARCHIVED`.
- Start the DLQ flow (`initiateDLQAndArchive`) for batches that move to `ARCHIVING` in both the local rollback (`rollbackOrProcessStateUpdates`) and the persister-failure path, outside the partition lock as in the successful path.
- Derive the DLQ cause from the delivery count when the batch has no recorded cause.

### Testing

- New `InFlightStateTest` (5 cases), which also fills the existing coverage gap for `completeStateTransition`:
  - normal release path at the limit -> `ARCHIVING` (baseline)
  - rollback with expired lock at the limit, DLQ enabled -> `ARCHIVING`
  - rollback with expired lock at the limit, DLQ disabled -> `ARCHIVED`
  - rollback with expired lock below the limit -> `AVAILABLE`
  - rollback without an expired lock restores the previous state and member
  - The DLQ-enabled rollback case fails on trunk and passes with this change.
- Regression: `SharePartitionTest` (289), `SharePartitionManagerTest` (60), `ShareGroupDLQStateManagerTest` (71), `ShareGroupDLQRecordFetcherTest` (29) - all pass with the change.
- `checkstyle` passes for the changed modules.

Reviewers: Sushant Mahajan <sushant.mahajan88@gmail.com>

issue_comments.body: @yixiaodan This was deliberately avoided as a persister fail => a 5 time call to persister with exponential backoff failed. Now with DLQ again, the first step is ARCHIVING which requires a persister write. This too has good chance of failing (same partition key, so same broker). Hence the decision was taken to not stall the in-flight records queue over this.

Thanks @smjn — understood, and thanks for the explanation.

Since the direct ARCHIVED transition is intentional to avoid stalling the in-flight queue when the persister has already failed after retries, I'll close this PR. I'll leave KAFKA-21380 open for the record. If useful, I can follow up separately with a narrower observability change (metric/log when records are archived on this path) rather than changing the state transition.

Thanks for the review.

commit.message:
KAFKA-21380: Move limit-reached records to ARCHIVING on failed transition rollback

When a two-phase state transition fails and the acquisition lock has
expired, completeStateTransition rolled records back to ARCHIVED
directly when the delivery count was at the limit, even when the DLQ
flow was enabled. Records that should have been dead-lettered were
silently archived and never appeared in the DLQ topic.

Thread the DLQ-support flag through the rollback path, mirroring the
normal transition path, and start the DLQ flow for batches that move
to ARCHIVING in both the local rollback and the persister-failure
paths.

The new InFlightStateTest covers the rollback path (previously
untested) alongside the normal release path and the DLQ-disabled case.
